content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've described this issue before, but I'm including more specifics now. I developed a program using a function block diagram in [product_name] and created a web page it controls in [product_name]. Viewing it on my PC's browser works perfectly since the [product_name] device is connected to my computer via ethernet. However, when I enter the [product_name] device's IP address in my mobile browser—regardless of browser—I receive a connection timeout. I realize my phone needs wireless access and must be on the same subnet as the [product_name] device to connect. Here's my current setup: [product_name] device IP is 192.168.20.22 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0, it's LAN-connected to my laptop (on WiFi, IPv4 192.168.20.21, subnet mask 255.255.255.0), and my phone is also on the same wireless network with IPv4 192.168.20.21. Yet, I get a connection timeout when entering 192.168.20.22 in my mobile browser. What steps should I take to access my web page with my mobile browser?
Try using 192.168.20.22:8080 in your browser. It's possible the necessary ports aren't open. Check your [product_name] device's port settings.
It looks like both your laptop and mobile phone have the same IP address set. Consider changing one—for example, set your mobile device's IP to 192.168.20.23.

Typically, if your [product_name] device is connected to a PC via ethernet cable, only that PC can access the [product_name] web server. To allow access from other devices, the [product_name] device must be part of a network available to those remote devices. Suggested steps: 1) Connect the [product_name] device to your local network with internet access—usually WiFi. Test if you can access the web server from WiFi. 2) Set up a VPN connection for external devices to reach your local network. 3) Confirm you can connect to the [product_name] device from your remote device over the internet. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face issues accessing the [product_name] web page from mobile devices, though PC access works when directly connected. The main challenge lies in network setup, especially direct Ethernet connections vs. a network accessible via WiFi. Confusion about correct IP assignments and port settings arises, but the core issue is related to configuring standard networking rather than a direct usability failure in the product.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to smoothly open the [product_name] device web page from any device on the same network, including smartphones over WiFi, without complicated changes to network configuration.
